title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Training Note: The Regular Hourly Rate for Holiday Pay
content:
**What is the regular hourly rate of a holiday-pay report?** On Unemployment Benefit Claims, it is the hourly rate at which holiday hours are valued, read from the certifications of the claimant's most recent earlier claim of the same program.

**Which terms are used?**

- *Window earnings* and *window hours*: the gross earnings and the hours worked on the earlier claim's certifications whose week ended within the history window, each added together.
- *The latest certified week*: the earlier claim's certification with the latest week ending date.

**How is the rate set?**

| Window hours | Latest certified week | Regular hourly rate |
|---|---|---|
| At least 60 (the minimum hours) | Any | Window earnings divided by window hours, rounded to the cent |
| Above zero but fewer than 60 | Reports hours worked | That week's earnings divided by its hours, rounded to the cent |
| Any other case | — | The earlier claim's high-quarter wages divided by 520 quarter hours, rounded to the cent |

**Hypothetical cases.**

- Window hours 64.0 and window earnings 1216.00: 19.00.
- Window hours 30.0; latest certified week 600.00 for 30.0 hours: 20.00.
- No certified hours in the window; high-quarter wages 9360.00: 18.00.
- Exactly 60.0 window hours with 1080.00 of earnings: 18.00 by the first row.
